eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket reflects tight clustering around 62-65°F for San Francisco's highest temperature on May 6, driven by National Weather Service forecasts projecting peaks in the low-to-mid 60s amid a persistent marine layer. Cool Pacific sea surface temperatures near 55°F sustain stratocumulus clouds and advection fog over the coast, capping diurnal warming by reducing solar insolation despite light onshore winds of 5-10 mph. Ensemble model runs from GFS and ECMWF show a 2-3°F spread, with 64-65°F slightly favored due to potential late-afternoon burn-off allowing modest heating, while stronger marine influence could limit to 62-63°F. Historical May highs average 65-67°F, but recent rainy patterns and rebuilding stratus favor the cooler outcomes. Watch NWS hourly updates for morning observations refining the peak.

Recent days saw verified highs of 34°C on May 3 and around 32-35°C on May 4-5 at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (WMKK), fueling trader consensus for outcomes in the 32-36°C range as stagnant air and high humidity enable heat buildup. Emerging El Niño patterns amplify regional warmth above May's climatological average of 32°C, but model discrepancies on shower timing create genuine uncertainty, reflected in tightly clustered market-implied probabilities; watch METMalaysia's daily update on May 6 for refined guidance.
